keyVerseText: And there he found a certain man named Aeneas, which had kept his bed eight years, and was sick of the palsy.
rootMeaning: The name Αἰνέας (Ainéas) is of uncertain derivation, with no clear root word or etymology provided. From the Strong's definition, it is identified simply as a proper noun referring to an Israelite individual. This lack of a known root meaning means that the name primarily serves as an identifying marker rather than conveying a descriptive or symbolic sense beyond the personal identity of the man named Aeneas.
usageInScripture: The word Αἰνέας occurs only twice in the New Testament and is consistently translated as "Aeneas," indicating a proper name with no variation in meaning or application. Both occurrences refer to the same individual, emphasizing a specific person rather than a concept or title. This consistency highlights that the term functions strictly as a personal identifier within the scriptural narrative.
theologicalSignificance: Though the name Αἰνέας itself does not carry an explicit theological meaning, its presence in Scripture as an identified Israelite who experiences healing underscores God's care for individuals within His covenant people. The mention of Aeneas by name in Acts reflects the personal nature of Christ's healing power and the extension of salvation and restoration to those who are physically afflicted. This reminds believers that God's redemptive work is not abstract but intimately involved with real people and their needs, affirming the value and dignity of each person in the body of Christ.
keyVerseReflection: Acts 9:33 states, "And there he found a certain man named Aeneas, which had kept his bed eight years, and was sick of the palsy." The use of the name Αἰνέας personalizes the account, drawing attention to the individual who experienced prolonged suffering and subsequent healing. Naming him invites readers to see the reality of God's miraculous work in a specific life, emphasizing that divine intervention reaches into the everyday struggles of believers.
